claims.text: IFLScience reports gastric juice can dissolve zinc.
claims.quote: Your gastric juice is capable of dissolving your organs, zinc, and the legs of living frogs

claims.text: The lining secretes thick mucus with bicarbonate, which protects it from digesting itself.
claims.quote: This mucus, along with bicarbonate, forms a protective layer that prevents the stomach from digesting itself; secretes a thick alkaline mucus, rich in bicarbonate

claims.text: The lining's cells are tightly joined together, part of the barrier.
claims.quote: the epithelial cells themselves, which are tightly joined together

claims.text: H. pylori's spiral shape and flagella let it move into the less acidic mucus lining.
claims.quote: The bacteria reach the less acidic mucosa by use of their flagella; Its helical shape is better suited for progressing through the viscous mucosa lining of the stomach

claims.text: About half the world's population carries H. pylori; most have no symptoms.
claims.quote: over half of the global population is infected, but most individuals are asymptomatic

claims.text: For decades ulcers were blamed on stress, spicy food and too much acid.
claims.quote: ulcers were caused primarily by stress, spicy foods, and too much acid; were caused by stress, spicy foods, and too much acid in the stomach

claims.text: In July 1984 Barry Marshall drank a broth of cultured H. pylori.
claims.quote: drank a broth containing cultured H; One July day in 1984, Barry Marshall

claims.text: About three days later he had nausea and bad breath, which his wife noticed.
claims.quote: only three days later, he developed vague nausea and halitosis; bad breath , noticed by his wife

claims.text: The 2005 Nobel Prize went for showing that gastritis and peptic ulcers are caused by H. pylori infection.
claims.quote: This year’s Nobel Laureates in Physiology or Medicine made the remarkable and unexpected discovery that inflammation in the stomach (gastritis) as well as ulceration of the stomach or duodenum (peptic ulcer disease) is the result of an infection of the stomach caused by the bacterium Helicobacter pylori

myths.myth: Ulcers are caused by stress and spicy food.
myths.truth: Most peptic ulcers are caused by H. pylori infection (2005 Nobel Prize).
